unit.title: From a Correct Algorithm to a Trustworthy ADT
unit.audience: A strong algorithms student who is already proficient in a programming language and is building practical software-engineering habits in Java.
learning_objectives: Turn behavioral requirements into a precise public contract for a small abstract data type.
Connect an abstraction function and representation invariant to implementation choices.
Defend an abstraction boundary against invalid input, arithmetic edge cases, and representation exposure.
Use example-based and model-based tests as durable evidence of behavior.
Make a bounded requirement change without weakening existing behavior or clarity.

included: Specifications, abstraction function, representation invariant, defensive design, tests, and one change request
Learner reflection through unanswered comprehension prompts
excluded: Any claim that this is an official MIT 6.031 unit
Official readings, lectures, problem sets, project content, or solutions

unit_complete_when: All implementation, test, design-note, change-log, and comprehension deliverables named in student_safe/STUDY_TASK.md are present.
A worker-harness-controlled validator confirms that the submitted program builds and its tests pass.
An examiner applies examiner_only/RUBRIC.md and records the required result independently of the learner's claims.

preparation.method: The manager used only the supplied catalog snapshot to bound and contextualize an original kickoff exercise.
preparation.authorship_note: The kickoff learning design and local packet are manager-authored, not MIT-authored or MIT-endorsed.
